SMTO-GWT-0057 — An interrupted file copy was cancelled, so nothing was copied

GUID: 7d6a8b66-d1ff-4e60-b31a-f3d51a44ffdc
Slug: transfer-staging-aborted
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • A file copy between two computers was interrupted. When SMTO picked the work back up, it safely cancelled the unfinished copy. The destination file was not created or replaced.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check that the source file is still the version you want copied. Time has passed since the interrupted copy, and the file may have changed in the meantime.
  2. Ask SMTO in the conversation to copy the file again. The old copy was cancelled before anything was written to the destination, so a new copy won't duplicate it.
  3. When it finishes, check that the destination folder has the file with the size you expect. This confirms the new copy, not the cancelled one, produced the file.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the new copy as copied and verified, and the file is in the destination folder.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the two Gateway computers. Don't ask SMTO to continue the old cancelled copy; start a new one with the file as it is now.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • On resume, transfer recovery received an aborted state or a successful destination_abort receipt for a pre-commit transfer and settled it as unpublished without re-sending any data; no destination file was published by that staging attempt.

What this means

  • Recovery obtained an aborted transfer state or a successful staging-abort receipt, so it settled the interrupted transfer as unpublished instead of repeating its data movement. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Recovery obtained an aborted transfer state or a successful staging-abort receipt, so it settled the interrupted transfer as unpublished instead of repeating its data movement.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the reconciled transfer state and cleanup_complete separately; compare the source revision before planning a new copy.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the transfer checkpoint (phase and recorded source revision) and confirm staging cleanup completed on the destination Gateway. Before a new gateway.copy, read the source's current revision instead of reusing the recorded expected_source_revision, because the source may have changed since the interrupted attempt.
  • Inspect the transfer checkpoint and source revision before starting a new transfer attempt.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The transfer remains reconciled as aborted, and any outstanding cleanup is confirmed before new transfer work.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
